usd_glossary_terms.definition: Activation is a metadatum/behavior of prims that models a 'non destructive and reversible prim deletion' from a stage. Prims are active by default, which means they and their active children will be composed and visited by stage traversals.
An API schema is a prim Schema that serves as an interface or API for authoring and extracting a set of related data, and may also contribute to a prim’s definition.
In USD an assembly is a kind of Model. Assemblies are group models, i.e. models that aggregate other models into meaningful collections.
Asset is a fairly common organizational concept in content-producing pipelines. In the most generic terms in USD, an asset is something that can be identified and located with a string identifier.
AssetInfo is a metadata dictionary that can be applied to any UsdPrim or UsdProperty to convey asset-identification-and-management-related information.
Asset resolution is the process by which an asset path is translated into the location of a consumable resource.
Attributes are the most common type of property authored in most USD scenes. An attribute can take on exactly one of the legal attribute typeNames USD provides.
Similarly to how prims can be deactivated through composing overriding opinions, the value that an attribute produces can be blocked by an overriding opinion of None.
See Connection.
See Variability.
Change processing is the action a UsdStage takes in response to edits of any of the layers that contribute to its composition.
Class is one of the three possible specifiers a prim (and also a primSpec) can possess.
See Value Clips.
Collections build on the ability of relationships to identify objects in a USD scene.
A component is a 'leaf' kind of Model. Components can contain subcomponents, but no other models.
Composition is the process that assembles multiple layers together by the composition arcs that relate them to each other.
Composition arcs are the 'operators' that allow USD to create rich compositions of many layers containing mixes of 'base' scene description and overrides.
Connections are quite similar to relationships in that they are list-edited 'scene pointers' that robustly identify other scene objects.
The crate file format is USD’s own binary file format, whose file extension is .usdc, and which is losslessly, bidirectionally convertible to the .usda text format.
Def is one of the three possible specifiers a prim (and also a primSpec) can possess.
Many assets consist entirely of a static definition, which really exists 'outside time'.
A direct opinion for some property or metadatum of a prim at path in a layerStack is one that is authored 'directly' on the primSpec.
When authoring composed scene description, it is often desirable to edit the targets of various composition arcs in context of the scene you are constructing.
Many IsA Schemas and applied API Schemas define attributes that have an identifiable value that makes sense in most situations.
Even though USD derives great efficiencies from accessing data directly from the layers that a stage composes together, it can sometimes be useful to 'bake down the composition' into a single layer.
Gprim comes from Pixar’s RenderMan terminology, and is a contraction for 'Geometric primitive'.
In USD a group is a kind of Model. Groups are models that aggregate other models into meaningful collections.
Hydra is a modern rendering architecture optimized for handling very large scenes and 'change processing'.
An index, also referred to as a PrimIndex, is the result of composition, and the primary piece of information we compute and cache for a composed prim on a stage.
Inherits is a composition arc that addresses the problem of adding a single, non-destructive edit that can affect a whole class of distinct objects on a stage.
Instanceable is a metadatum that declares whether a given prim should be considered as a candidate for instancing.
Instancing in USD is a feature that allows many instances of 'the same' object to share the same representation on a UsdStage.
Interpolation appears in two different contexts in USD: Temporal Interpolation of values in attribute value resolution and Spatial Interpolation of Primvar values across a gprim.
An IsA schema is a prim Schema that defines the prim’s role or purpose on the Stage.
Kind is a reserved, prim-level metadatum whose authored value is a simple string token.
A Layer is the atomic persistent container of scene description for USD.
Composition arcs such as References and SubLayers can include an offset and scaling of time to be applied during attribute value resolution for all data composed from the target layer.
LayerStacks are the keystone to understanding composition in USD.
List editing is a feature to which some array-valued data elements in USD can subscribe.
LIVERPS is an acronym for Local, Inherits, VariantSets, Relocates, References, Payload, Specializes, and is the fundamental rubric for understanding opinions and namespace compose in USD.
The Payload arc provides a 'deferred reference' behavior.
USD allows the construction of highly referenced and layered scenes that assemble files from many different sources.
Metadata is the lightest-weight form of (name, value) scene description.
Model is a scenegraph annotation ascribable to prims by setting their kind metadata.
Model Hierarchy builds on the concept of model in a scenegraph to tackle the problem of discovering and defining a 'table of contents of important subtrees of prims'.
Namespace is simply the term USD uses to describe the set of prim paths that provide the identities for prims on a Stage.
Opinions are the atomic elements that participate in Value Resolution in USD.
Over is one of the three possible specifiers a prim can possess.
A path is a location in namespace.
All of USD’s Composition Arcs other than SubLayers allow a 'prim name change' as the target prim of the arc gets composed under the prim that added the composition arc.
A Payload is a composition arc that is a special kind of a Reference.
A Prim is the primary container object in USD.
A prim definition is the set of built-in properties and metadata that a prim gains from a combination of the IsA schema determined from its typeName and its applied API schemas.
Each composed Prim on a Stage is the result of potentially many PrimSpecs each contributing their own scene description to a composite result.
A PrimStack is a list of PropertySpecs that contribute a default or timeSample for a given property.
The name primvar comes from RenderMan, and stands for 'primitive variable'.
Properties are the other kind of namespace object in USD.
Just as PrimSpecs contain data for a prim within a layer, PropertySpecs contain the data for a property within a layer.
A PropertyStack is a list of PropertySpecs that contribute a default or timeSample for a given property.
Proxy is a highly overloaded term in computer graphics.
A Stage’s PseudoRoot Prim is a contrivance that allows every UsdStage to contain a single tree of prims rather than a forest.
Purpose is a builtin attribute of the UsdGeomImageable schema.
After SubLayers, References are the next most-basic and most-important composition arc.
A Relationship is a 'namespace pointer' that is robust in the face of composition arcs.
Relocates is a composition arc that maps a prim path defined in a remote LayerStack to a new path location in the local namespace.
Every Stage has a 'root' LayerStack, comprised of the LayerStack defined by the root Layer on which the Stage was opened.
USD defines a schema as an object whose purpose is to author and retrieve structured data from some UsdObject.
Each UsdStage can be created with a session layer that provides for 'scratch space' to configure, override, and experiment with the data contained in files backing the stage.
Specializes is a composition arc that allows a specialized prim to be continuously refined from a base prim.
Every PrimSpec possesses a specifier, which conveys the author’s intent for how the PrimSpec should be consumed and interpreted in a composed scene.
A stage is the USD abstraction for a scenegraph derived from a root USD file.
Most consumption of USD data follows the pattern of traversing an open stage.
Subcomponent is another kind value like component that can be applied to a prim.
SubLayers is the composition arc used to construct LayerStacks.
TimeCodes are the unit-less time coordinate in USD.
For a composed scene, TimeCode coordinate values from TimeSamples are scaled to real-time seconds.
The term timeSample is used in two related contexts in USD.
Synonym for IsA Schema.
userProperties: is a property namespace recognized by the majority of DCC plugins as a place to look for 'extra custom properties'.
Value Clips are a feature that allows one to partition varying attribute timeSample overrides into multiple files.
Value Resolution is the algorithm by which final values for properties or metadata are composed from all of the various PropertySpecs or PrimSpecs.
Attributes possess a special piece of metadata called variability that serves as a statement of intent.
A variant represents a single, named variation of a VariantSet.
A VariantSet is a composition arc that allows a content creator to package a discrete set of alternatives.
